items.item_text: Background Check: Continued employment is contingent upon the completion of a satisfactory background investigation.
Bachelor's Degree In related area and / or equivalent experience / training
PhD PhD or equivalent in biological sciences
Master's Degree In related area and / or equivalent experience / training
Experience in immunofluorescent techniques and flow cytometer operations with human and non-human animal cells including embryonic and other pluripotent stem cells.
Experience in operating a fluorescence activated cell sorter and fluorescence activated cell analyzers
Experience in an immunologic laboratory performing cell surface staining with monoclonal antibodies and flow cytometric analysis.

The Lab Research Specialist 5 will perform professional work in support of biological scientific research and contribute to the development of research goals for the Owen Witte laboratory in the Department of Microbiology, Immunology & Molecular Genetics (MIMG). Working collaboratively with the investigator, the incumbent will determine the most suitable methods to be used in research; independently perform scientific investigative procedures requiring application of professional judgment; interpret experimental results and determine whether they are consistent with experimental goals; review pertinent literature for information that will further research goals; and prepare reports of research for presentation or publication. The incumbent will be expected to perform flow cytometric analyses and fluorescence activated cell sorting using multi-laser cell sorters on human and non-human animal cells including embryonic and other pluripotent stem cells to find, characterize and isolate stem cells and progenitors from both mouse and human origins. Work with investigators to establish experimental design. Maintain flow cytometer's peak performance and optimize instrument configurations for specialized investigations. Operate and maintain FACS instruments, coordinate instrument service and trouble-shoot problems. Maintain accurate experimental and machine quality control (Q.C.) records, including Biosafety measurement for aerosol containment. Perform and train investigators in data analysis using specialized software programs. Develop mechanisms for tracking instrument use, Flow Resource SOPs, applications, and user qualifications.
College level courses in most of the following areas: biology, biochemistry, immunology.
Skill in laboratory safety protocols including handling and disposal of infectious specimens.
Skill in asceptic techniques including working with cells, microliter volumes and centrifuges.

Skill in reading and following instructions in laboratory protocols and other scientific documents; skill in creating and editing lab SOPs, applications, and user qualifications; oral and written technical and non-technical communication skills.
Skill to train others and cooperate with a research team; skill in providing appropriate education and training of users.
Skill in math including computing ratios, percentages.

Ability to perform effectively under conditions of fluctuating workload and with frequent distractions; skill in organization and priority setting which accurately reflects the relative importance of tasks; ability to modify work schedule.

Skill in working with minimal supervision to carry out assigned work. Skill in recognizing problems and aberrant results and taking appropriate action including asking questions or notifying the laboratory supervisor.
Skill in the use of balance and pH meter for solution preparation.
Skill in performing non-human animal model surgeries and related tissue preparation.
